# iris-vpu-dkms Debian Packaging

This directory contains the Debian packaging for the `iris-vpu-dkms`
binary package. The package installs the Iris VPU out-of-tree kernel
module source under `/usr/src/iris-vpu-<version>` and manages DKMS
registration, build, installation, and removal through `dh_dkms`.

The package also installs modprobe policy that blocks `qcom_iris` and
regenerates initramfs on install and removal. It does not actively unload
or load kernel modules from maintainer scripts.

## Layout

- `control`: package metadata and build/runtime dependencies.
- `rules`: debhelper entry point. It installs only the files needed for
  DKMS builds instead of copying the whole source tree.
- `iris-vpu-dkms.dkms`: points `dh_dkms` at the DKMS configuration file.
- `dkms.conf`: DKMS module configuration. `dh_dkms -V` rewrites
  `PACKAGE_VERSION` to the package upstream version during build.
- `iris-vpu-dkms.install`: installs package-managed module policy files.
- `modprobe.d/iris-vpu-dkms.conf`: package-managed blacklist for
  `qcom_iris`.
- `postinst`: triggers initramfs regeneration after package
  configuration so the blacklist is included in the boot image.
- `postrm`: triggers initramfs regeneration after package removal so the
  blacklist is removed from the boot image.

## Build Host Dependencies

Install the Debian packaging tools before building the package:

```sh
sudo apt update
sudo apt install dpkg-dev debhelper dh-dkms
```

The authoritative build dependencies are listed in `debian/control`:

```text
Build-Depends: debhelper-compat (= 13), dh-sequence-dkms
```

`dpkg-buildpackage` is provided by `dpkg-dev`. `dh_dkms` is provided by
the distribution DKMS debhelper integration package, commonly `dh-dkms`
or a package that provides `dh-sequence-dkms`.

## Build

Run the package build from the repository root:

```sh
cd pkg-video-driver
dpkg-buildpackage -us -uc -B -aarm64
```

The generated binary package is written to the parent directory of the
source tree, for example:

```text
iris-vpu-dkms_<version>_arm64.deb
```

The build also writes `.changes` and `.buildinfo` files to the same
parent directory.

## Clean

Clean the packaging build tree from the repository root:

```sh
dpkg-buildpackage -Tclean -aarm64
```

Use the same host architecture that was used for the build. Because this
package is `Architecture: arm64`, running `debian/rules clean` or
`dpkg-buildpackage -Tclean` on an amd64 build host can make debhelper skip
package-specific cleanups as an architecture mismatch.

On an arm64 build host, this is also sufficient:

```sh
dpkg-buildpackage -Tclean
```

This removes debhelper-generated files under `debian/`. It does not
remove previously generated `.deb`, `.changes`, or `.buildinfo` files
from the parent directory; remove those manually when they are no longer
needed.

## Build Flow

During `override_dh_install`, `debian/rules` creates:

```text
debian/iris-vpu-dkms/usr/src/iris-vpu-<version>/
```

and copies the DKMS build inputs:

- `Makefile`, generated from `debian/dkms-Makefile`
- `Kbuild`
- `driver/`
- `video/`
- `include/`
- `config/`
- `dkms.conf`, installed by `dh_dkms`

The source files are copied from an explicit allowlist so the package
contains the DKMS inputs without copying unrelated repository files.

The generated `Makefile` is a DKMS-safe wrapper. It prepares the source
layout at DKMS build time and then invokes the kernel external module
build:

- generates `driver/vidc/inc/video_generated_h`
- creates or refreshes `video/driver -> ../driver`
- calls `make -C /lib/modules/<kernel-version>/build ... modules`

The wrapper does not remove `video/driver` after the build, so manual
`make` from `/usr/src/iris-vpu-<version>` does not damage the DKMS source
tree.

## Target Platform Dependencies

Runtime package dependencies are generated by debhelper and `dh_dkms`.
The source dependency list in `debian/control` is:

```text
Depends: linux-initramfs-tool, ${misc:Depends}
```

`${misc:Depends}` adds the DKMS runtime dependency generated by
`dh_dkms`.

Before installing the package on a target platform, ensure the platform
has:

- `dkms`
- an initramfs tool provider, such as `initramfs-tools` on Ubuntu
- matching kernel headers or kernel build tree for the running kernel
- normal DKMS build toolchain packages pulled in by the distribution
  `dkms` package, such as compiler and make support

The target system must provide:

```sh
/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build
```

If this path is missing or points at incomplete headers, the package can
install but DKMS cannot build `iris_vpu.ko` for the running kernel.

Prefer installing the local `.deb` with `apt` so dependencies are
resolved automatically:

```sh
sudo apt install ./iris-vpu-dkms_<version>_arm64.deb
```

If `dpkg -i` is used instead, install dependencies first or repair them
afterwards:

```sh
sudo apt update
sudo apt install dkms initramfs-tools
sudo dpkg -i ./iris-vpu-dkms_<version>_arm64.deb
```

`linux-initramfs-tool` is a virtual package in Debian/Ubuntu. It is valid
in `debian/control`, but when preinstalling dependencies by hand, select
a real provider. On Ubuntu, use `initramfs-tools`.

If `dpkg -i` was already run before the dependencies were installed,
repair the partial installation with:

```sh
sudo apt -f install
```

`dpkg -i` does not resolve missing dependencies by itself. A dependency
error such as `iris-vpu-dkms depends on dkms` means either use
`sudo apt install ./iris-vpu-dkms_<version>_arm64.deb` or install `dkms`
before running `dpkg -i`.

## Install On Target

Copy the generated package to the target platform and install it with:

```sh
sudo apt install ./iris-vpu-dkms_<version>_arm64.deb
```

During installation, the package:

- installs DKMS source under `/usr/src/iris-vpu-<version>`
- registers the module with DKMS
- builds and installs `iris_vpu.ko` for the running kernel
- installs `/usr/lib/modprobe.d/iris-vpu-dkms.conf`
- blacklists `qcom_iris`
- maps explicit `modprobe qcom_iris` requests to `/bin/false`
- triggers initramfs regeneration so the policy also applies after reboot

The package does not automatically unload `qcom_iris` or load
`iris_vpu`. If a runtime switch is required without rebooting, do it
explicitly after checking platform state:

```sh
sudo modprobe -r qcom_iris
sudo modprobe iris_vpu
```

If `qcom_iris` is in use, `modprobe -r qcom_iris` can fail. Stop the
userspace clients that hold the device before unloading the module.

## Verify Install

Check package installation:

```sh
dpkg -s iris-vpu-dkms
```

Check DKMS state:

```sh
dkms status -m iris-vpu
```

Check that the built module is visible:

```sh
modinfo iris_vpu
```

Check that the package-managed modprobe policy is installed:

```sh
test -f /usr/lib/modprobe.d/iris-vpu-dkms.conf
modprobe --showconfig | grep -A2 -B2 qcom_iris
```

An installed package should show policy equivalent to:

```text
blacklist qcom_iris
install qcom_iris /bin/false
```

Check runtime module state if needed:

```sh
lsmod | grep -E 'iris_vpu|qcom_iris'
```

`iris_vpu` appears in `lsmod` only after it is loaded by platform policy,
manual `modprobe`, or device probing. A successful package install does
not require `iris_vpu` to already be loaded.

## Uninstall From Target

Remove the package with:

```sh
sudo apt remove iris-vpu-dkms
```

or:

```sh
sudo dpkg -r iris-vpu-dkms
```

During removal, DKMS removes the registered `iris-vpu` module build and
the package removes `/usr/lib/modprobe.d/iris-vpu-dkms.conf`. The package
also triggers initramfs regeneration so the blacklist is removed from the
boot image.

To remove package configuration state as well:

```sh
sudo apt purge iris-vpu-dkms
```

The package does not automatically unload `iris_vpu` or load
`qcom_iris` during removal. If a runtime switch is required without
rebooting, do it explicitly after package removal:

```sh
sudo modprobe -r iris_vpu
sudo modprobe qcom_iris
```

## Verify Uninstall

Check that the package is no longer installed:

```sh
dpkg -s iris-vpu-dkms
```

`dpkg -s` should report that the package is not installed.

Check that DKMS no longer has the module registered:

```sh
dkms status -m iris-vpu
```

Check that the package-managed blacklist file is gone:

```sh
test ! -e /usr/lib/modprobe.d/iris-vpu-dkms.conf
```

Check that this package no longer blocks `qcom_iris`:

```sh
modprobe --showconfig | grep -A2 -B2 qcom_iris
```

There should be no `blacklist qcom_iris` or
`install qcom_iris /bin/false` entry from `iris-vpu-dkms`. If another
package or local admin file still blocks `qcom_iris`, remove that policy
from the owning package or local configuration.

## DKMS Handling

DKMS registration, build, install, and removal are handled by
`dh_dkms`. `debian/rules` calls `dh_dkms -V` so the
`#MODULE_VERSION#` placeholder in `debian/dkms.conf` is replaced with
the package upstream version when `dkms.conf` is installed under
`/usr/src/iris-vpu-<version>`.

The installed `dkms.conf` invokes the DKMS source tree `Makefile`
wrapper. The wrapper prepares `video_generated_h` and `video/driver`,
then invokes the kernel external module build interface with
`make -C /lib/modules/<kernel-version>/build` and points `M`,
`KERNEL_SRC`, and `VIDEO_ROOT` at the DKMS source tree.

The `make` command is quoted in `dkms.conf` so DKMS does not prepend its
own `KERNELRELEASE=<kernel-version>` argument. This avoids routing DKMS
builds through a default `all` target that may require `vmlinux` from an
incomplete kernel headers tree.

The package does not generate compatibility headers for the target
kernel. Headers required by the kernel external module build, including
V4L2 and time headers, must be provided by the target kernel headers
package.

## Module Policy

The package installs package-managed modprobe policy for `qcom_iris`
under `/usr/lib/modprobe.d` and triggers initramfs regeneration on
install and removal so the policy is honored during early boot. The
policy blacklists automatic loading and maps explicit `modprobe
qcom_iris` requests to `/bin/false`. The package does not actively unload
or load modules from maintainer scripts. Boot-time loading and runtime
module changes are left to the platform configuration or administrator.

## Troubleshooting

If installation fails with dependency errors, use `apt` to install the
local package:

```sh
sudo apt install ./iris-vpu-dkms_<version>_arm64.deb
```

or repair a partial `dpkg -i` install:

```sh
sudo apt -f install
```

If DKMS build fails, inspect the DKMS build log:

```sh
sudo less /var/lib/dkms/iris-vpu/<version>/build/make.log
```

If the log shows missing kernel headers, missing generated kernel files,
or type/header failures such as missing `sys/time.h`, `bool`, or
`size_t`, fix the target kernel headers package. This Debian packaging
does not generate replacement kernel compatibility headers.

If the log includes:

```text
ERROR (dkms apport): kernel package ... is not supported
```

use `make.log` as the source of truth. The apport message is commonly a
secondary report after the DKMS build command has already failed.

If `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build` is missing, install the matching
kernel headers or fix the target kernel package so that path points at a
valid kernel build tree.

If `modinfo iris_vpu` fails after DKMS reports a successful build, run:

```sh
sudo depmod -a
modinfo iris_vpu
```

`depmod -a` is normally handled by DKMS/module installation paths, but it
is useful when debugging module lookup state.

If initramfs regeneration prints warnings such as:

```text
Warning: root device does not exist
System running in EFI mode, skipping.
```

check the final package install exit status first. These warnings come
from the platform initramfs tooling. If the package installed
successfully, verify that the expected `/boot/initrd.img-<kernel-version>`
or platform boot image update exists according to the target distro's
boot flow.
